Lomza New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Łomża, Poland

Not demolished. This is the newer of Łomża's two Jewish cemeteries, established around 1890. In 1910, Rabbi Malkiel Tannenbaum, a noted halakhic authority, was buried here; his grave remains marked by a partially ruined architectural tombstone along the main alley. During WWII, the Germans executed both Jews and Poles at the cemetery, and its funeral house was later converted into apartments. In 1992, in connection with a visit by Israeli President Chaim Herzog, municipal authorities cleaned up the site; since 1999, it has been cared for by the Łomża Jewish Cemetery Foundation.
